name: forward_projector
summary: Emit future-adjacent forward chains. Inline extraction from controlled models (free, instant) + post-hoc fallback via tiny model (qwen2.5-coder:1.5b via ollama, ~10s). The projection is what feeds the next inference node as context.
engine_pattern: stateless — given (reasoning_trace, output_text, prev_forward) returns ForwardResult(inline, posthoc, source, chosen)

modes.inline: regex <forward>(.*?)</forward> against the just-completed output; placeholder bodies rejected (literal '...', single phrases, empty)
modes.posthoc: subprocess ollama run <tiny_model> with stdin pipe + dumb TERM + CSI cursor-back interpretation; bounded by CC_FORWARD_TIMEOUT (default 20s)

tty_artifact_handling: _strip_ansi interprets CSI \x1b[<N>D (cursor back N — pops up to N chars from output buffer, stops at newlines), drops other CSI codes silently, then a (\\S{2,})\\n(\\1\\S*) regex collapses any wrap-fragment-then-redraw pairs
substrate: none (consumes reasoning + output, produces forward_chain text)

inbound_callers: CLI: python3 forward_projector.py inline | posthoc | project
outbound_calls: subprocess.run(['ollama', 'run', <tiny_model>], input=prompt) — only when posthoc fallback fires
routing_connections.substrate_writes: none (projector is pure; chat.py persists the result)

guarantees: Inline extraction is byte-deterministic (regex on the model's literal output)
Posthoc projection runs only when inline returns empty (lazy)
Graceful degradation — missing ollama / timeout / parse error → returns empty string, never raises
No TTY artifacts persisted — cursor-back interpretation + wrap-repeat regex run before storage
usage_example: from forward_projector import project\nresult = project(reasoning_trace='I read X then edited Y', output_text='Done. <forward>- step1\\n- step2</forward>', prev_forward='', enable_posthoc=True)\nprint(result.source, result.chosen())  # -> 'inline', '- step1\\n- step2'
